name: Temporal Prediction
text:
# Temporal Prediction
## Overview
Temporal prediction compresses time-varying volume data by [exploiting temporal coherence](#5560-exploiting-temporal-coherence-c-buffer.md) between frames [S1]. It distinguishes itself from sibling methods like [Spatial Predictive Coding](12623-spatial-predictive-coding.md) by operating across time steps, and from [Residual Coding for Volumetric Compression](6518-residual-coding-for-volumetric-compression.md) by its specific focus on frame-to-frame dependencies in dynamic datasets [G].
## Shared principles
The methods share a common pipeline: predicting the current frame from a reference frame, computing a residual, quantizing the residual, and entropy coding it [S1]. Closed-loop reconstruction is required when using [delta encoding](#1096-delta-encoding.md) to prevent error accumulation across time steps [G].
## Subtopics

### [Delta Encoding](1096-delta-encoding.md)
Operates directly in the spatial-temporal domain without prior transform steps, relying on unchanged regions producing zero-valued residuals. Choose when data exhibits high spatial-temporal coherence and uniform bricks can be exploited for [compression](#4-compression.md).

### [Residual Updates in Transform Domain](5256-residual-updates-in-transform-domain.md)
Operates in the frequency domain (e.g., [DCT](#8014-discrete-cosine-transform-dct.md)), estimating current frame's transform coefficients from the previously reconstructed frame's coefficients. Choose when volumetric changes are smooth and frequency-domain concentration of residual energy improves compressibility.

### [MPEG-like Time-Variant Encoding](13596-mpeg-like-time-variant-encoding.md)
Applies lossy MPEG encoding principles to time-varying data, allowing high compression ratios and [fast rendering](#11491-interactive-forward-rendering-with-approximate-splatting.md) via texture mapping hardware. Choose when hardware-accelerated [on-the-fly decompression and rendering](#10013-adapt-decompress-draw-rendering-pipeline.md) are available.

### [Difference encoding for time-variant volumes](13616-difference-encoding-for-time-variant-volumes.md)
Transforms data in the temporal domain by computing first- and second-order differences for each voxel's time series. Choose when temporal redundancy at individual spatial locations is high and entropy coding can exploit clustered coefficient distributions.

### Inter-frame Delta Encoding with Haar Wavelets
Classifies each time step as an intra-coded or predictive frame [S1]. All frames are encoded with Haar wavelets, but predictive frames are additionally expressed as deltas with respect to previous frames before encoding [S1].

### Dynamic Rendering with Advection
Augments a sample prediction network to take current time as input, outputs velocities to advect sample points to the nearest keyframe time using a forward-Euler step, and renders final color by summing over samples at the advected positions [S2].

## Background
Temporal prediction techniques have been applied to compressed GPU-based [direct volume rendering](#1184-direct-volume-rendering.md) to handle dynamic datasets [S1]. Early approaches included packing three time steps into RGB channels for 3D-RGB compression [S1] and classifying frames as intra-coded or predictive, encoding predictive frames as deltas with respect to previous frames using Haar wavelets [S1]. Subsequent methods performed delta encoding on block data with respect to the previous time step, quantizing blocks based on data range and encoding with LZO [S1], or performing delta encoding followed by [hierarchical vector quantization](#827-hierarchical-vector-quantization.md) [S1].
## Sources
[S1] A Survey of Compressed GPU-Based Direct Volume Rendering, https://www.ifi.uzh.ch/dam/jcr:00000000-7f10-48e5-ffff-ffff94c9f943/CompressedDVR.pdf, fetched 2026-10-27
[S2] HyperReel: High-Fidelity 6-DoF Video with Ray-Conditioned Sampling, https://doi.org/10.1109/cvpr52729.2023.01594, fetched 2026-10-26
